**Phase 2 checkpoint** — committed `9a582282`.

## Landed
- **`pathland-engine`**: `Gesture` gained `ValueInput`/`TextInput`/`DateInput` sinks (+ handler type aliases); `InputHandlers` + `collect_input_handlers` expose the app-side registries; `WritableSignal::set` writes the store; fixed `Bool` signal packing to raw `0/1` (the boolean properties are `U8`).
- **`pathland-view`**: two-way controls bind a writable signal, record a sink, and set the `BINDING_ID` gate:
  - `TextField`/`TextEditor` `t.text(sig)`, `Toggle` `t.is_on(sig)`, `Slider`/`Stepper` `s.bind(sig)` (initial read from the signal), `Picker` `p.bind(sig)`;
  - `Button::action(f)` wires the tap + pointer listeners.
- **GTK demo**: a two-way name `TextField`; the host routes `TEXT_CHANGED` into the input sink and re-emits to flush the bound node.
- `status.md` (engine + view) and the spec status delta updated.

## Verified
`cargo test --workspace` green; `check-wasm.sh` OK; no new clippy warnings.

## Next — Phase 3: styles + environment
Two parts, both new to Rust:
- **Environment**: a typed `EnvironmentKey`/`EnvironmentValues` subtree scope. Java uses a thread-local; `no_std` can't, so I'll use an explicit scope carried through build (engine-owned or a `BuildContext`). This is the one flagged decision.
- **Styles**: `Style`/`ButtonStyle`/`LabelStyle`/`AudioStyle`/`VideoStyle` reading the shared `V::Config` from the environment; built-in `PlainButtonStyle`/`BorderedButtonStyle`, `DefaultLabelStyle`/…; Button content precedence (child > title > style); plus GTK Composite Override Mode wiring.

All phases complete. The Rust DSL now implements the DSL v2 design, on branch `spec/dsl-v2-authoring-surface`.

## Commits
```
766b064a feat(view): persisted state (phase 5)
820650c2 feat(view): structural reactivity + navigation (phase 4)
a7de5465 feat(view): styles + environment (phase 3)
9a582282 feat(engine,view): two-way control bindings + actions (phase 2)
5299c2b2 feat(engine,view): reactive runtime — signals, computed, effects (phase 1)
89c63e10 feat(engine,view): typed signals + text/property binding (phase 1a)
11860ce1 feat(view): DSL v2 authoring surface (phase 0)
8e99c806 spec(dsl): v2 authoring surface
```

## Delivered
- **Phase 0** — three operations (`with`/`modifiers`/`children`, static+chained, any order), per-view `Config`, single/tuple `ModifierList`, no `Mod` suffix, named shapes.
- **Phase 1** — a shared `no_std` **`Runtime`** (`Rc<RefCell<Store>>`, no thread-local): value + **computed** + **effect** signals, `untracked`, typed handles, text/property binding; GTK demo made reactive.
- **Phase 2** — **two-way bindings** (input sinks + `BINDING_ID`; TextField/TextEditor/Toggle/Slider/Stepper/Picker) and **actions** (`Button::action`); `collect_input_handlers`; demo two-way field.
- **Phase 3** — **`Environment`** threaded through `View::build_env`; **`ButtonStyle`** (`Plain`/`Bordered` + custom) via `ViewExt::button_style`.
- **Phase 4** — **`Conditional::when`**, **`RouteTable`/`Router`/`NavigationContainer`/`NavigationLink`**.
- **Phase 5** — **`StateStore` + `InMemoryStateStore` + `PersistentState`/`State<T>`** auto-load/auto-save.

## Verified each phase
`cargo test --workspace` green (pathland-view: 57 unit + 4 doctests; engine reactive tests); `check-wasm.sh` OK (`no_std` preserved); no new clippy warnings; no wire changes.

## Documented remaining gaps (`status.md`)
- Renderer event coverage for Stepper/TextEditor/DatePicker/ColorPicker; date/color two-way (needs `SET_DATE`).
- Styles limited to `ButtonStyle` (Rust has no Label/Audio/Video); environment is not arbitrary typed keys.
- Navigation links hold a router explicitly (no nearest-router resolution/`NavigationIntent`); `NAVIGATE` routing is app-side; no `Label`/`GridRow` components.
- Only the in-memory state backend.

## Note
The **Java DSL** still uses the old authoring surface — it hasn't been migrated to the v2 spec, and `AGENTS.md` still describes the old signatures. That's the natural next effort if you want cross-language convergence.

1121: 
1122: ## 8. Java DSL convergence (adopted)
1123: 
1124: The Java DSL (`com.pathland.view`) has the complete surface. The convergence
1125: below has been **adopted**: construction through the three operations
1126: (`with` / `modifiers` / `children`), and modifiers as `ViewModifier` values with
1127: **no `Mod` suffix** and **no per-modifier sugar on `View`**. The canonical
1128: contract is [§4](#4-view-surface) and [§5](#5-modifier-surface).
1129: 
1130: | Canonical | Java (adopted) | Optional / remaining |
1131: |-----------|----------------|----------------------|
1132: | `Text("…")` | `Text.with(t -> t.text("…"))` (String or `Signal<String>`) | — |
1133: | `Button("…", action)` / `Button(action:label:)` | `Button.with(b -> b.title("…").action(action))` and/or `.children(label)` | — |
1134: | `Toggle("label", isOn: writable)` | `Toggle.with(t -> t.label("…").isOn(writable))` | — |
1135: | `Slider(value: in:)` | `Slider.with(s -> s.value(writable).min(..).max(..))` (binding in config) | — |
1136: | `.border(color, width)` | `Border.with(b -> b.color(..).width(..))` via `.modifiers(...)` | radius convenience on the same builder |
1137: | `DatePicker(selection:)` | `DatePicker.with(d -> d.mode(..).selection(days))` | *optional* `Date`-shaped config encoding days + millis-of-day per `SET_DATE`/`DATE_CHANGED` |
1138: 
1139: Adopted conventions:
1140: 
1141: - **`with` / `modifiers` / `children` are the one construction path.** Every
1142:   concrete view/control exposes these three operations; `.of(...)` is gone.
1143:   They are available **at creation or chained, in any order**
1144:   ([§2](#2-canonical-signature-notation)).
1145: - **`with(config)` is a fluent config builder.** The config holds the view's
1146:   values and is the same type a style's `makeBody(Config)` reads
1147:   ([§5.7](#57-styleable-controls-the-style-contract)).
1148: - **The `View.*` static-factory surface is removed.** The entire factory block
1149:   (`text`, `image`, `rectangle`, `spacer`, `vstack`, `hstack`, `zstack`,
1150:   `button`, `textField`, `textEditor`, `toggle`, `slider`, `stepper`,
1151:   `progressView`, `gauge`, `divider`, `grid`, `scrollView`, `lazyVStack`,
1152:   `lazyHStack`, `lazyVGrid`, `lazyHGrid`, `picker`, `menu`, `colorPicker`,
1153:   `datePicker`, `group`) is deleted from `View.java`.
1154: - **`Group` is a first-class view.** `Group.with().children(View...)` is a
1155:   transparent container view (SwiftUI `Group`).
1156: - **Core and custom modifiers share one mechanism.** Core modifiers are
1157:   `ViewModifier` values (`Padding.with(p -> p.uniform(16))`,
1158:   `ForegroundStyle.with(f -> f.color(color))`) applied via `.modifiers(...)` —
1159:   there is **no sugar on `View`**; several modifiers at once use
1160:   `.modifiers(...)`, innermost-first. Single-value modifiers pass the value
1161:   directly (`FontWeight.BOLD`).
1162: - **No `Mod` suffix.** A modifier type is named for the modifier it applies;
1163:   where it wraps a single value, the value type is the modifier. Main's
1164:   `FrameMod → Frame` (with the wire batch renamed `emit.Frame → ProtocolFrame`)
1165:   is the precedent; the remaining `*Mod` types are renamed accordingly
1166:   (`FontWeightMod → FontWeight`, `ButtonStyleMod → ButtonStyle`, …;
1167:   `EnvironmentMod → EnvironmentBinding`, `router/NavigationMod → NavigationIntent`).
1168: - **Full `ShapeKind` coverage.** `Circle.with()`, `Capsule.with()`,
1169:   `Ellipse.with()`, `RoundedRectangle.with(r -> r.cornerRadius(..))`, generic
1170:   `Shape.with(s -> s.kind(ShapeKind))` (for `Path`).
1171: - Implementation status: `lib/java/pathland-view/status.md`.
1172: 
1173: ---
1174: 
1175: ## 9. Generation contract for a new language
1176: 
1177: An AI (or a human) generating a Pathland DSL in a new language MUST produce the
1178: following and verify each item. This is a checklist; the authoritative details
1179: are the companion specs.
1180: 
1181: ### 9.1 Required surface
1182: 
1183: - [ ] **Views/controls** — every entry of [§4](#4-view-surface):
1184:   `Text`, `Image`, `Color`, `Shape` (all `ShapeKind`s), `Divider`, `Spacer`,
1185:   `ProgressView`, `Gauge`; `VStack`, `HStack`, `ZStack`, `Grid`, `GridRow`,
1186:   `ScrollView`,
1187:   `LazyVGrid`, `LazyHGrid`, `LazyVStack`, `LazyHStack`; `Button`,
1188:   `TextField`, `SecureField`, `TextEditor`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Stepper`,
1189:   `Picker`, `Menu`, `DatePicker`, `ColorPicker`.
1190: - [ ] **The three operations** — configure values, apply modifiers, supply
1191:   children — available at creation or by chaining, in any order
1192:   ([§2](#2-canonical-signature-notation)). Each language maps them to its idiom
1193:   ([§9.3](#93-language-adaptation-rules)).
1194: - [ ] **Modifiers** — every entry of [§5](#5-modifier-surface), applicable to
1195:   any view, innermost-first, emitting one property per underlying argument; a
1196:   modifier's type carries no `Mod` suffix.
1197: - [ ] **Custom modifiers / unified mechanism** — a `ViewModifier` authoring
1198:   surface (`body(content) -> View`) + a chainable `modifiers(...)` operation on
1199:   **any** view; **core modifiers are implemented through the same mechanism**,
1200:   never a separate syntax ([§5.6](#56-custom-modifiers-developer-authored)).

# pathland-view (Java) — implementation status

**Last updated:** September 14, 2026

The hand-written, framework-agnostic Java 17+ DSL (`com.pathland.view`):
declarative views, Angular-style signals, fine-grained emitter, `PLPL` wire
codec, lazy JNA ring interop, and cross-platform `State`. Protocol contract:
`spec/`. Runs on every LTS from Java 17.

## Implemented

- **`SizeThatFits` fit slot** (`SizeThatFits.of(Fit...)` + `Fit.of(view, minWidth)`):
  a structural slot (`SIZE_THAT_FITS` 0x17) emitting `FIT_QUERY` (LIST, ascending
  thresholds) + the single selected child — unselected candidates never transmit.
  The host routes `FIT_CHANGED` into the slot's fit sink
  (`RenderResult.fitInputs`, via `InputDispatcher`), which swaps the child through
  the structural reconcile (an unchanged index re-emits zero opcodes). The LIST
  value type is written by `FrameOpcodeSink`/`RingOpcodeSink`
  (`[count][f32 × count]` arena entries). A slot's selection is **retained node
  state** (`PathlandNode.fitSelection`): a parent-subtree re-render (an outer
  slot's candidate swap, a custom style body re-run) may rebuild a nested slot
  with a default index, so the reconcile **carries the previous selection across
  the match** (`Emitter.restoreFitSelection`) — a nested fit (the player bar's
  controls slot under the root row) keeps its candidate instead of resetting to
  compact (a reset would strand the DOM client, which never re-reports an
  unchanged width).
- **Construction is `.of()` only**: every concrete view/control exposes a
  static `<ViewName>.of(...)` factory (`Text.of`, `VStack.of`,

## Java migration scope (measured)

Java is **feature-complete** — signals, styles, navigation, state, the emitter all exist. So unlike Rust, this is a **surface-only** migration (the v2 authoring API), not new features.

Current surface to replace:
- **116** classes with a static `.of(...)` factory; **68** `ViewModifier` impls; **15** `*Mod` classes; `View` sugar methods (`font`, `navigate/push/replace`, `environment`, `onPathChange`); styles use `makeBody(Configuration)` records.

## Proposed Java plan (phased)

- **J0 — infrastructure + construction:** add a `Config` base, the static-or-chained mechanism, `View.modifiers(...)`/`children(...)`, and the static `with(config)` template. Convert primitives + containers (`Text/Image/Icon/Color/Shape`+named/`Divider/Spacer/ProgressView/Gauge`, `VStack/HStack/ZStack/Grid/GridRow/ScrollView/Lazy*/SizeThatFits/Group`) and the leaf modifier factories (`.of` → `.with`).

- **J2 — styles:** `Style extends ViewModifier`; `ButtonStyle/LabelStyle/AudioStyle/VideoStyle.makeBody(V.Config)`; built-ins re-based on the shared config.
- **J3 — no `Mod` suffix:** rename the 15 types; value-is-modifier where possible (`FontWeight.BOLD`, `FontStyle.ITALIC`, `TextAlignment.CENTER`, `Truncation.TAIL`, `TextCase.UPPERCASE`, `ControlSize.LARGE`, `Font.headline()`, `ButtonStyle`); `EnvironmentMod → EnvironmentBinding`, `router/NavigationMod → NavigationIntent`; delete `View` sugar.

# Plan: Java DSL v2 authoring-surface migration

## Nature of the work
Java is **feature-complete** (signals, styles, navigation, state, emitter all exist). This is a **surface-only** migration to the `spec/DSL.md` §8 contract — no new features, no wire change.

## The generic builder mechanism
```java
// one type, reused by every view
public final class ViewBuilder<V extends View & Configurable<C>, C extends View.Config>
        implements View {
    V with(Consumer<C> configure);          // re-configure the view's values
    ViewBuilder<V,C> modifiers(ViewModifier... m);   // innermost-first
    ViewBuilder<V,C> children(View... c);   // content-bearing views only (typed)
    PathlandNode render(Environment env);   // set children, render, apply modifiers
}
```
- `View.Config` — a nested marker base; each view exposes `V.Config` and implements `Configurable<C>` (`C config()`).
- **Statics on the view class** (any is a valid entry, any order): `Text.with(c -> …)`, `Text.modifiers(m…)`, `Text.children(v…)` → each returns a `ViewBuilder<Text, Text.Config>`.
- The **view class holds no instance** `with`/`modifiers`/`children` (avoiding Java's static-hides-instance rule); the chain lives on the builder. Custom views still implement `View` and are wrapped via the builder when needed.

## Library migration (`pathland-view`) — one atomic change (hard cut ⇒ can't compile incrementally)
- **`View`**: remove `.with(ViewModifier...)` and the sugar (`font`, `navigate`/`push`/`replace`, `environment`, `onPathChange`); add `View.Config` base + `Configurable`/`ChildrenView` markers; `Modified`/`ViewBuilder` host modifier application.
- **Views → `with(config)`** (`§4`): primitives (`Text/Image/Icon/Color/Shape`+named/`Divider/Spacer/ProgressView/Gauge/Label`), containers (`VStack/HStack/ZStack/Grid/GridRow/ScrollView/Lazy*/SizeThatFits/Group`), controls (`Button/TextField/SecureField/TextEditor/Toggle/Slider/Stepper/DatePicker/Picker/Menu/ColorPicker`). Delete every `.of(...)`. `Button` content precedence: **child > config title > style content**.
- **Modifiers → `Modifier.with(config)` / bare value** (`§5`): all 68 `ViewModifier` impls; `Padding.with(p -> p.uniform(16))`, `Frame.with(f -> …)`, etc.
- **No `Mod` suffix** (value-is-modifier): `FontWeight`, `FontStyle`, `TextAlignment`, `TextCase`, `Truncation`, `ControlSize`, `FontDesign` (enums implement `ViewModifier`), `Font`, and the styles become modifiers; `EnvironmentMod → EnvironmentBinding`, `router/NavigationMod → NavigationIntent`. `FontMod → Font` merge.
- **Styles → shared config + modifier** (`§5.7`): `Style extends ViewModifier`; `ButtonStyle/LabelStyle/AudioStyle/VideoStyle.makeBody(V.Config)` reads the control's `Config`; built-ins (`PlainButtonStyle`/`BorderedButtonStyle`, `DefaultLabelStyle`/`TitleOnly`/`IconOnly`, `NativeAudio`/`VideoStyle`) re-based; `ButtonStyle` applied via `.modifiers(MyButtonStyle)`.
- **Delete** the `View.*` static-factory block (`text`, `vstack`, …).
- Update the library's own tests in the same change.

## Consumer migration (each module compiles against the migrated library)
Order by size: `pathland-demo-views` (422/172) → `pathland-server-core` (80) → `pathland-render-html` (38/5) → `pathland-quarkus-starter`/`pathland-spring-boot-starter` → `pathland-test-kit` → gtk/qt/tui demos + the two boot demos.

## Docs
`pathland-view/status.md` (construction is `with`/`modifiers`/`children`, not `.of()`), and **`AGENTS.md`** (the Java sections still describe the old surface + Rust `Text.of`).

## Verification
`cd lib/java && mvn install` (full reactor) after the library change, then again after each consumer; run the Quarkus/Spring demos; cross-check that the wire output is unchanged (existing Java tests + `spec/CONFORMANCE.md`).

## Risks
- The library is **not green until the whole atomic change lands** (hard cut) — one large, carefully reviewed change.
- `ViewBuilder` generics (`V extends View & Configurable<C>`) are verbose; mitigated by one reusable type + 2–3 generated-ish statics per view.
- Environment/style scoping must keep working through the builder (styles wrap as modifiers → environment binding path).

## Objective
- Rework the Pathland DSL authoring surface ("DSL v2"): spec-first, then implement in the Rust DSL, and now migrate the Java DSL (`com.pathland.view`) to the same contract.
- DSL v2: every view exposes three order-independent operations — values via static `View.with(config)`, modifiers via `.modifiers(...)`, children via `.children(...)`, each usable at creation or chained in any order; per-view config shared with styles; no `Mod` suffix (value-is-modifier).

## Important Details
- Working branch: `spec/dsl-v2-authoring-surface` (created off `main`). Working tree clean after last commit; not pushed.
- Design decisions (locked, user-approved):
  - **Spec-first**; `spec/DSL.md` is the contract. `with`/`modifiers`/`children` replace `.of(...)`/`.with(...)`; config builder shared with styles; no `Mod` suffix; Button content precedence child > config title > style content.
  - Per-language adaptation (§9.3): Java/C# `with`/`With`; Rust assoc-fn + trait + macros; Go package ctor + methods; Python kwargs (`with` is a keyword). Names are recommendations; operations/semantics are the contract.
  - §9.3 matrix: value-is-modifier via Java/Rust/Python enums, Go typed const+method, C# record struct (enums can't implement interfaces).
- Rust design choices: generic `Runtime` (`Rc<RefCell<Store>>`, no thread-local) for signals; `Environment` threaded via `View::build_env(&self, env)`; `Modified<V>` wrapper; `ModifierList` single/tuple; `Gesture::Tap/ValueInput/TextInput/DateInput` sinks.
- **Java decisions (just confirmed):** (1) generic `ViewBuilder<V,C>`; (2) **hard cut** (no `@Deprecated` shims; tree won't compile mid-migration); (3) library-first then consumers; (4) nested `V.Config` names.
- Java has NO annotation-based config; no `V.Config` exists anywhere.
- User asked to "compact first" — compaction is a client action; not doable from here, proceeding anyway.
- Do NOT run workspace-wide `cargo fmt` (repo is not rustfmt-clean; caused 48-file churn once, reverted). Prefer avoiding `perl`/`sed` for edits.
- No wire/protocol changes in any phase; `check-wasm.sh` must stay green for Rust (pathland-core/pathland-engine/pathland-view are `#![no_std]` + alloc).

### Completed
- **Spec** (`spec/DSL.md` rewrite, commit `8e99c806`): three operations, §9.3 language-adaptation table (Java/C#/Rust/Go/Python), no-`Mod` rule, config-shared-with-styles, Button precedence. 9: /**
10:  * A view wrapped by one or more property modifiers (innermost-first) or a custom
11:  * {@link ViewModifier}. Property modifiers apply to the innermost built node and are
12:  * overwritten by outer modifiers ("outermost wins"); reactive modifiers record
13:  * a node-level binding so a signal change re-emits only that property.
14:  */
15: final class Modified implements View {
16: 
17:     /** One property application: a static value or a reactive signal. */
18:     record Prop(int property, Object value, Signal<?> signal) {
19: 
20:         static Prop value(int property, Object value) {
21:             return new Prop(property, value, null);
22:         }
23: 
24:         static Prop reactive(int property, Signal<?> signal) {
25:             return new Prop(property, null, signal);
26:         }
27:     }
28: 
29:     private final View inner;
30:     private final List<Prop> props;
31:     private final ViewModifier modifier;
32: 
33:     private Modified(View inner, List<Prop> props, ViewModifier modifier) {
34:         this.inner = inner;
35:         this.props = props;
36:         this.modifier = modifier;
37:     }
38: 
39:     /** A static property mod. */
40:     static Prop prop(int property, Object value) {
41:         return Prop.value(property, value);
42:     }
43: 
44:     /** A reactive property mod. */
45:     static Prop prop(int property, Signal<?> signal) {
46:         return Prop.reactive(property, signal);
47:     }
48: 
49:     /** Build a property-modifier view from inner + props. */
50:     static Modified props(View inner, Prop... props) {
51:         return new Modified(inner, List.of(props), null);
52:     }
53: 
54:     /** A custom-view-modifier wrapper. */
55:     static Modified apply(View inner, ViewModifier modifier) {
56:         return new Modified(inner, List.of(), modifier);
57:     }
58: 
59:     @Override
60:     public PathlandNode render(Environment env) {
61:         if (modifier != null) {
62:             return modifier.body(inner).render(env);
63:         }
64:         PathlandNode node = inner.render(env);
65:         for (Prop p : props) {
66:             if (p.signal() != null) {
67:                 Object value = ReactiveValues.from(p.property(), p.signal());
68:                 node.properties.put(p.property(), value);
69:                 node.propertyBindings.put(p.property(), p.signal());
70:             } else {
71:                 node.properties.put(p.property(), p.value());
72:             }
73:         }
74:         return node;
75:     }
76: }

3: import com.pathland.view.emit.PathlandNode;
4: 
5: /**
6:  * An interactive button ({@code Button}). Accepts an arbitrary child view as
7:  * the label. The control owns the native {@code BUTTON} node and wires the action on
8:  * it (whole button tappable, including its padding); the active {@link ButtonStyle}
9:  * (spec DSL.md §5.7) supplies the button's content — the label, decorated — as the
10:  * button node's child, so a composite label keeps its own layout.
11:  */
12: public final class Button implements View {
13: 
14:     private final View label;
15:     private final Runnable action;
16: 
17:     private Button(String title, Runnable action) {
18:         this(Text.of(title), action);
19:     }
20: 
21:     private Button(View label, Runnable action) {
22:         this.label = label;
23:         this.action = action;
24:     }
25: 
26:     /** A button with a plain text title. */
27:     public static Button of(String title, Runnable action) {
28:         return new Button(title, action);
29:     }
30: 
31:     /** A button with an arbitrary child view as its label. */
32:     public static Button of(View label, Runnable action) {
33:         return new Button(label, action);
34:     }
35: 
36:     @Override
37:     public PathlandNode render(Environment env) {
38:         // The control owns the native BUTTON shell + the action; the style supplies
39:         // the content (the decorated label) as the shell's child. The label keeps its
40:         // own component(s) and layout (Composite Override Mode, PRIMITIVES.md §2).
41:         PathlandNode node = new PathlandNode(Components.BUTTON);
42:         ButtonStyle style = env.buttonStyle();
43:         View content = style.makeBody(new ButtonStyle.Configuration(label));
44:         if (content != null && content != EmptyContent.INSTANCE) {
45:             node.children.add(content.render(env));
46:         }
47:         Object existing = node.properties.get(Properties.EVENT_LISTENERS);
48:         int mask = existing instanceof Integer i ? i : 0;
49:         node.properties.put(
50:                 Properties.EVENT_LISTENERS,
51:                 mask | Commands.Listeners.POINTER_DOWN | Commands.Listeners.POINTER_UP);
52:         node.tapActions.add(action);
53:         return node;
54:     }
55: }

130: ## 2. Canonical signature notation
131: 
132: The canonical signatures below are written SwiftUI-shaped and language
133: agnostic. Conventions used:
134: 
135: - `View(config:)` / `T("…")` — a view/control constructed with its **values**.
136: - `{ ... }` — the child subtree (a trailing closure in SwiftUI; a vararg,
137:   macro, builder, or lambda in other languages).
138: - `Signal<T>` — a read-only derived or writable signal; `WritableSignal<T>` —
139:   a two-way binding target. A control takes a `WritableSignal<T>` for its
140:   value (see [§3](#3-state-model-signals)).
141: - `()` — the action a `Button` fires.
142: - `.modifier(m)` — apply a **modifier value** to a view; chainable on any
143:   view. Every modifier — built-in or application-authored — is such a value
144:   ([§5.6](#56-custom-modifiers-developer-authored)).
145: - Modifiers chain and are applied **innermost-first** (the last chained
146:   modifier's property wins).
147: 
148: ### The three operations
149: 
150: Every concrete view exposes the same three operations. They form one fluent
151: **builder**: any of the three may be the first call, and they may be chained in
152: any order. A later call overrides an earlier value for the same property.
153: 
154: | Operation | Purpose | Canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) |
155: |-----------|---------|----------------------------|
156: | **values** | Configure structural/layout values and a control's bound value | `View(config:)` — labels in the constructor |
157: | **modifiers** | Apply `ViewModifier` values, innermost-first | `.modifier(_:)` / `.padding(_:)` / … |
158: | **children** | Supply the content subtree (content-bearing views only) | trailing closure `{ … }` |
159: 
160: The **canonical builder spelling** (the recommended form; per-language spellings
161: are in [§9.3](#93-language-adaptation-rules)) is:
162: 
163: ```
164: ViewName.with { values }              // values   — a config-builder lambda
165:       .modifiers(modifier, ...)       // modifiers — varargs
166:       .children(view, ...)            // children  — varargs, content-bearing views only
167: ```
168: 
169: Any of the three may start the chain, e.g. all of these are equivalent:
170: 
171: ```
172: VStack.with { v in v.spacing(8) }.children(a, b).modifiers(m)
173: VStack.children(a, b).with { v in v.spacing(8) }.modifiers(m)
174: VStack.modifiers(m).children(a, b).with { v in v.spacing(8) }
175: ```
176: 
177: **Values are a config-builder lambda.** `with { c in … }` populates a per-view
178: fluent **config** (`VStack.Config`, `Text.Config`, …). The config accepts raw
179: values **or** `Signal`s (so `c.text(signal)` stays reactive) and is the *same
180: type* a style's `makeBody(Config)` receives ([§5.7](#57-styleable-controls-the-style-contract)).
181: The builder is **fluent and mutable**: setters return the config. Config-less
182: views (`Divider`, `Spacer`) take an empty `with()`.
183: 
184: **Per-language realization.** Java cannot declare a static and an instance
185: method with the same signature, so the Java realization holds the three
186: statically on the view class and exposes the chainable forms on the returned
187: builder/view type. Other languages map the operations to their idioms
188: (extension methods, associated functions + traits, package constructors +
189: methods, kwargs) — see [§9.3](#93-language-adaptation-rules).
190: 
191: Per-language adaptation summary:
192: 
193: | Language | Case | Composition mechanism | Example |
194: |----------|------|-----------------------|---------|
195: | SwiftUI | `camelCase` | trailing closures + result builder | `VStack(alignment: .center, spacing: 8) { Text("x").padding(16) }` |
196: | Java (`com.pathland.view`) | `camelCase` | `with(Consumer)` builder + `modifiers(...)` + `children(...)` | `VStack.with(v -> v.spacing(8)).children(Text.with(t -> t.text("x")).modifiers(Padding.with(p -> p.uniform(16))))` |
197: | Rust (`pathland-view`) | `snake_case` | assoc fn + `ViewExt` trait + macros | `vstack![text("x").modifiers(Padding(16.0))]` |
198: 
199: ---
200: 
201: ## 3. State model (signals)
202: 
203: Pathland state is **Angular-style signals**. This is the non-negotiable
204: reactive core every DSL exposes.
205: 
206: ### 3.1 Signal surface
207: 
208: | Canonical | Java DSL (`com.pathland.view.signal`) | Semantics |
209: |-----------|--------------------------------------|-----------|
210: | `signal(initial)` | `Signals.signal(T)` | a writable signal |
211: | `signal(name, initial)` | `Signals.signal(String, T)` | named (names surface in dependency errors) |
212: | `signal(initial, equal)` | `Signals.signal(T, BiPredicate<T,T>)` | custom equality |
213: | `computed(fn)` | `Signals.computed(Supplier<T>)` | lazy, memoized derived signal |
214: | `effect(fn)` | `Signals.effect(Runnable)` | runs immediately, then on dependency change |
215: | `untracked(fn)` | `Signals.untracked(Supplier<T>)` | reads without recording dependencies |
216: | `read()` | `get()` | current value |
217: | `write(v)` | `set(T)` | replace (no-op when equal) |
218: | `update(fn)` | `update(UnaryOperator<T>)` | derive from current and write |
219: | `asReadonly()` | `asReadonly()` | read-only view of a writable signal |
220: 
221: **Guarantees** (must be preserved by any implementation): equality suppression,
222: synchronous flush at the end of the outermost write, glitch-free propagation
223: (each computed recomputes at most once per flush), error caching, write
224: discipline, and circular-dependency detection.
225: 
226: ### 3.2 Two-way binding
227: 
228: A control's value is **a `WritableSignal<T>` supplied as a config value**:
229: `TextField.with(t -> t.placeholder("…").text(writable))`,
230: `Toggle.with(t -> t.isOn(writable))`,
231: `Slider.with(s -> s.value(writable).min(0).max(100))`. The flow:
232: 
233: 1. At **mount**, the DSL control records a **value input** (a sink on the
234:    retained node) for the signal, and the emitter exposes routing registries to
235:    the host: tap actions, text inputs, value inputs, date inputs.
236: 2. The host receives the control's raw event (`TEXT_CHANGED`,
237:    `VALUE_CHANGED`, `DATE_CHANGED`, or a composed tap) and calls the sink,
238:    which **writes into the signal**.
239: 3. The signal flush re-emits **only that node's** delta (`SET_TEXT`,
240:    `SET_PROPERTY`, `SET_DATE`) back through the emitter.
241: 
242: Reading is equally fine-grained: a node's text or a property value can be
243: **bound to a signal** — `Text.with(t -> t.text(signal))`,
244: `.modifiers(ForegroundStyle.with(f -> f.color(colorSignal)), FontSize.with(s -> s.size(sizeSignal)))`
245: — so a change re-emits only the bound node.
246: 
247: ### 3.3 Persisted state (`State<T>`)
248: 
249: A `State<T>` field is the SwiftUI-`@State`-shaped form of a persisted signal,

689: ## 5. Modifier surface
690: 
691: Properties, value types, and emission rules come from
692: [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md); the tables here give the **DSL signature**. A
693: compound SwiftUI modifier expands to **one `SET_PROPERTY` per underlying
694: property** (`.frame` → `WIDTH` + `HEIGHT` + `ALIGNMENT`; `.border` →
695: `BORDER_COLOR` + `BORDER_WIDTH`; `.shadow` → `SHADOW_COLOR` + `SHADOW_RADIUS` +
696: `SHADOW_X` + `SHADOW_Y`). The `Java DSL` column is the reference realization.
697: 
698: ### 5.0 Authoring a modifier
699: 
700: **One mechanism for every modifier.** Each entry below is a `ViewModifier`
701: value, applied through the shared `modifiers(...)` operation:
702: 
703: - **Parameterized modifiers** are created with `Modifier.with(c -> …)` (a fluent
704:   config builder), e.g. `Padding.with(p -> p.uniform(16))`,
705:   `Frame.with(f -> f.width(100).height(24))`.
706: - **Single-value modifiers** — a font, a font weight, an alignment, a style —
707:   may pass the value directly, because the value type *is* the modifier: `FontWeight.BOLD`,
708:   `TextAlignment.CENTER`, `Font.headline()`, `MyButtonStyle`.
709: - A modifier's type is **never** suffixed with `Mod` (§1).
710: 
711: ```java
712: Text.with(t -> t.text("hi")).modifiers(
713:         Padding.with(p -> p.uniform(16)),
714:         Frame.with(f -> f.width(100).height(24)),
715:         FontWeight.BOLD,
716:         ForegroundStyle.with(f -> f.color(Color.WHITE)));
717: ```
718: 
719: ### 5.1 Layout & frame
720: 
721: | Modifier | Canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) | Java DSL | Property(ies) |
722: |----------|---------------------------|----------|---------------|
723: | `frame` | `.frame(width:height:alignment:)` | `.modifiers(Frame.with(f -> f.width(w).height(h).alignment(a)))` — the 2D `Alignment` positions the content within the box; omitted → no `ALIGNMENT` emitted, a stack's own alignment is preserved | `WIDTH` 0x100B, `HEIGHT` 0x100C, `ALIGNMENT` 0x0002 (only when provided) |
724: | `frame(min:…)` | `.frame(minWidth:idealWidth:maxWidth:minHeight:idealHeight:maxHeight:)` | `.modifiers(Frame.with(f -> f.minWidth(..).idealWidth(..).maxWidth(..).minHeight(..).idealHeight(..).maxHeight(..)))` (the `Frame.Builder`; unset bounds are omitted — NaN/∞ = no limit) | `MIN_WIDTH` 0x0012 … `MAX_HEIGHT` 0x0017 |
725: | `padding` | `.padding(_:)` / `.padding(_:edges:)` | `.modifiers(Padding.with(p -> p.uniform(float)))` / `.modifiers(Padding.with(p -> p.edges(t, r, b, l)))` | `PADDING` 0x1011 / `PADDING_TOP` 0x1012 … `PADDING_LEFT` 0x1015 |
726: | `offset` | `.offset(x:y:)` | `.modifiers(Offset.with(o -> o.x(float).y(float)))` | `OFFSET_X` 0x000E, `OFFSET_Y` 0x000F |
727: | `position` | `.position(x:y:)` | `.modifiers(Position.with(p -> p.x(float).y(float)))` | `POSITION_X` 0x0010, `POSITION_Y` 0x0011 |
728: | `fixedSize` | `.fixedSize()` / `.fixedSize(horizontal:vertical:)` | `.modifiers(FixedSize.with())` / `.modifiers(FixedSize.with(f -> f.horizontal(boolean).vertical(boolean)))` | `FIXED_SIZE_HORIZONTAL` 0x0018, `FIXED_SIZE_VERTICAL` 0x0019 |
729: | `layoutPriority` | `.layoutPriority(_:)` | `.modifiers(LayoutPriority.with(l -> l.value(float)))` | `LAYOUT_PRIORITY` 0x001A |
730: | `zIndex` | `.zIndex(_:)` | `.modifiers(ZIndex.with(z -> z.value(float)))` | `Z_INDEX` 0x100F |
731: | `aspectRatio` | `.aspectRatio(_:contentMode:)` | `.modifiers(AspectRatio.with(a -> a.ratio(float).contentMode(ContentMode)))` | `ASPECT_RATIO` 0x001B, `CONTENT_MODE` 0x001C |
732: | `scaledToFit` | `.scaledToFit()` | `.modifiers(ScaledToFit.with())` | `CONTENT_MODE` 0x001C (Fit) |
733: | `scaledToFill` | `.scaledToFill()` | `.modifiers(ScaledToFill.with())` | `CONTENT_MODE` 0x001C (Fill) |
734: | `minimumScaleFactor` | `.minimumScaleFactor(_:)` | `.modifiers(MinimumScaleFactor.with(m -> m.value(float)))` | `MINIMUM_SCALE_FACTOR` 0x001D |
735: 
736: **Semantics**: `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` use the sentinels `FILL` (−1.0 = expand) and
737: `HUG_CONTENT` (−2.0 = intrinsic); omitting an axis leaves it to the native
738: renderer. SwiftUI's `.frame(maxWidth: .infinity)` / `maxHeight: .infinity` is
739: written by passing `Float.POSITIVE_INFINITY` (Java) / `f32::INFINITY` (Rust) to
740: the width/height builder members, which is normalized to `FILL` before emission.
741: In the min/ideal/max builder an infinite `maxWidth`/`maxHeight` means *no limit*
742: (the bound is omitted). `OFFSET` is a post-layout translation; `POSITION` is
743: absolute placement within the parent.
744: 
745: ### 5.2 Text formatting
746: 
747: | Modifier | Canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) | Java DSL | Property(ies) |
748: |----------|---------------------------|----------|---------------|
749: | `font` | `.font(.system(size:))` | `.modifiers(Font.with(f -> f.system(float)))` / `Font.with(f -> f.system(size, weight, design))` | `FONT_SIZE` 0x1007 (+ `FONT_WEIGHT`/`FONT_DESIGN` when given) |
750: | `font` (predefined) | `.font(.largeTitle)` | `.modifiers(Font.headline())` (the `Font` value *is* the modifier) | `TEXT_STYLE` 0x1032 |
751: | `fontWeight` | `.fontWeight(_:)` | `.modifiers(FontWeight.BOLD)` (the enum *is* the modifier) | `FONT_WEIGHT` 0x1008 (100–900) |
752: | `font` (custom) | `.font(.custom(name:size:))` | `.modifiers(Font.with(f -> f.custom("Georgia", 20)))` | `FONT_FAMILY` 0x1009 |
753: | `fontStyle` | `.italic()` / `.fontDesign(_:)` | `.modifiers(Italic.with())` / `.modifiers(FontStyle.ITALIC)` / `.modifiers(FontDesign.SERIF)` | `FONT_STYLE` 0x1017, `FONT_DESIGN` 0x1018 |
754: | `fontWidth` | `.fontWidth(_:)` | `.modifiers(FontWidth.with(w -> w.value(float)))` | `FONT_WIDTH` 0x1019 |
755: | `kerning` | `.kerning(_:)` | `.modifiers(Kerning.with(k -> k.value(float)))` | `KERNING` 0x101A |
756: | `tracking` | `.tracking(_:)` | `.modifiers(Tracking.with(t -> t.value(float)))` | `TRACKING` 0x101B |
757: | `baselineOffset` | `.baselineOffset(_:)` | `.modifiers(BaselineOffset.with(b -> b.value(float)))` | `BASELINE_OFFSET` 0x101C |
758: | `lineSpacing` | `.lineSpacing(_:)` | `.modifiers(LineSpacing.with(l -> l.value(float)))` | `LINE_SPACING` 0x101D |
759: | `lineLimit` | `.lineLimit(_:)` | `.modifiers(LineLimit.with(l -> l.value(int)))` | `LINE_LIMIT` 0x000B (0 = unlimited) |
760: | `multilineTextAlignment` | `.multilineTextAlignment(_:)` | `.modifiers(TextAlignment.CENTER)` (the enum *is* the modifier) | `TEXT_ALIGNMENT` 0x000C |
761: | `truncationMode` | `.truncationMode(_:)` | `.modifiers(Truncation.TAIL)` (the enum *is* the modifier) | `TRUNCATION_MODE` 0x000D |
762: | `textCase` | `.textCase(_:)` | `.modifiers(TextCase.UPPERCASE)` (the enum *is* the modifier) | `TEXT_CASE` 0x101E |
763: | `underline` | `.underline()` | `.modifiers(Underline.with())` / `.modifiers(Underline.with(u -> u.enabled(boolean)))` | `UNDERLINE` 0x101F |
764: | `strikethrough` | `.strikethrough()` | `.modifiers(Strikethrough.with())` / `.modifiers(Strikethrough.with(s -> s.enabled(boolean)))` | `STRIKETHROUGH` 0x1020 |
765: | `foregroundStyle` | `.foregroundStyle(_:)` | `.modifiers(ForegroundStyle.with(f -> f.color(Color)))` / `.modifiers(ForegroundStyle.with(f -> f.color(Signal<Color>)))` | `COLOR` 0x100A |
766: | `tint` | `.tint(_:)` | `.modifiers(Tint.with(t -> t.color(Color)))` | `TINT` 0x1030 |
767: 
768: > **`Color` is never a modifier** — there is no `.color()` and
769: > `.foregroundColor(_:)` is deprecated. Foreground styling is
770: > `.foregroundStyle(_:)`.
771: 
772: ### 5.3 Appearance & effects
773: 
774: | Modifier | Canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) | Java DSL | Property(ies) |
775: |----------|---------------------------|----------|---------------|
776: | `background` | `.background(_:)` | `.modifiers(Background.with(b -> b.color(Color)))` / `.modifiers(Background.with(b -> b.color(Signal<Color>)))` | `BACKGROUND_COLOR` 0x1001 |

2: 
3: **Last updated:** September 14, 2026
4: 
5: The hand-written, framework-agnostic Java 17+ DSL (`com.pathland.view`):
6: declarative views, Angular-style signals, fine-grained emitter, `PLPL` wire
7: codec, lazy JNA ring interop, and cross-platform `State`. Protocol contract:
8: `spec/`. Runs on every LTS from Java 17.
9: 
10: ## Implemented
11: 
12: - **`SizeThatFits` fit slot** (`SizeThatFits.of(Fit...)` + `Fit.of(view, minWidth)`):
13:   a structural slot (`SIZE_THAT_FITS` 0x17) emitting `FIT_QUERY` (LIST, ascending
14:   thresholds) + the single selected child — unselected candidates never transmit.
15:   The host routes `FIT_CHANGED` into the slot's fit sink
16:   (`RenderResult.fitInputs`, via `InputDispatcher`), which swaps the child through
17:   the structural reconcile (an unchanged index re-emits zero opcodes). The LIST
18:   value type is written by `FrameOpcodeSink`/`RingOpcodeSink`
19:   (`[count][f32 × count]` arena entries). A slot's selection is **retained node
20:   state** (`PathlandNode.fitSelection`): a parent-subtree re-render (an outer
21:   slot's candidate swap, a custom style body re-run) may rebuild a nested slot
22:   with a default index, so the reconcile **carries the previous selection across
23:   the match** (`Emitter.restoreFitSelection`) — a nested fit (the player bar's
24:   controls slot under the root row) keeps its candidate instead of resetting to
25:   compact (a reset would strand the DOM client, which never re-reports an
26:   unchanged width).
27: - **Construction is `.of()` only**: every concrete view/control exposes a
28:   static `<ViewName>.of(...)` factory (`Text.of`, `VStack.of`,
29:   `Button.of(label, action)`, `Slider.of(binding, min, max)`,
30:   `DatePicker.of(mode, days)`, …); constructors are private and the former
31:   `View.*` static-factory surface is **removed**. `Slider`/`Stepper` are
32:   binding-first (initial value read from the signal); `Toggle` also offers the
33:   label-first `of(label, isOn)` overload; `Color.of(int)` alias. Grids take

content.text:
Java library migration (this turn): built the v2 surface end-to-end in `lib/java/pathland-view`, additive so the build stays green.

**Infrastructure** (`com.pathland.view`): `View.Config` marker, `Configurable<C>`, `ChildrenView`, and `ViewBuilder<V,C>` implementing the three chainable ops (`with`/`modifiers`/`children`, any order). `View` keeps only `body()`/`render()`.

**Views converted to `with`/`modifiers`/`children`** (legacy `.of` kept as a bridge): `Text`, `VStack`, `HStack`, `ZStack`, `Grid`, `GridRow`, `ScrollView`, `Group`, `LazyVStack`, `LazyHStack`, `LazyVGrid`, `LazyHGrid`, all shapes (`Shape`/`Rectangle`/`Circle`/`Ellipse`/`RoundedRectangle`/`Capsule`), `Image`, `Icon`, `Divider`, `Spacer`, `ProgressView`, `Gauge`, `Label`, `Button`, `TextField`, `TextEditor`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Stepper`, `Picker`, `DatePicker`, `Menu`, `ColorPicker`, `Audio`, `Video`.

**Modifiers**: added `Modifier.with(c -> …)` + `Config` for `Padding`, `ForegroundStyle`, `Opacity`, `Frame` (`Frame.with`), `FontSize`, `FontFamily`, `Background`, `Border`, `CornerRadius`, `LineLimit`, `Tint`, `ZIndex`, `Blur`, `Saturation`, `Contrast`, `Brightness`, `Grayscale`, `Rotation`, `ScaleEffect`, `Kerning`, `Tracking`, `BaselineOffset`, `LineSpacing`, `FontWidth`, `HueRotation`, `MinimumScaleFactor`, `LayoutPriority`, `Offset`, `Position`, `FixedSize`, `AspectRatio`, `ColorMultiply`, `ClipShape`, `Shadow`, `Visible`, `Disabled`, `AllowsHitTesting`, `Underline`, `Strikethrough`, `AccessibilityLabel/Role/State`, `PointerEvents`, `ActionId`, `BindingId`, `ImageSource`, `TapGesture`, plus no-value `with()` on `ColorInvert`/`Clipped`/`Hidden`/`ScaledToFit`/`ScaledToFill`/`Italic`.

**Value-is-modifier** (spec §5.0): `FontWeight`, `TextAlignment`, `Truncation`, `TextCase`, `ControlSize`, `FontStyle`, `FontDesign` now implement `ViewModifier`, and `Font` itself is the modifier. `Style extends ViewModifier`, so `ButtonStyle`/`LabelStyle`/`AudioStyle`/`VideoStyle` scope their env key via `.modifiers(style)`.

Verification: `mvn -o -pl pathland-view test` → **136 tests, 0 failures** (added `ViewBuilderTest`, `ModifierWithTest`). `status.md` updated.

Remaining: migrate consumers (`pathland-demo-views` ~422 `.of`/172 `.with`, `pathland-server-core`, `pathland-render-html`, starters, `*-demo`), convert `SizeThatFits`/`Conditional`/`NavigationContainer`/`NavigationLink`/`Color`, then delete the legacy `.of`/`View.with` shims and the now-redundant `*StyleMod`/`FontMod`/`*WeightMod` classes.

Want me to continue into the consumer modules, or commit this checkpoint first?
commit now. And lts discuss reactivity before we continue

201: ## 3. State model (signals)
202: 
203: Pathland state is **Angular-style signals**. This is the non-negotiable
204: reactive core every DSL exposes.
205: 
206: ### 3.1 Signal surface
207: 
208: | Canonical | Java DSL (`com.pathland.view.signal`) | Semantics |
209: |-----------|--------------------------------------|-----------|
210: | `signal(initial)` | `Signals.signal(T)` | a writable signal |
211: | `signal(name, initial)` | `Signals.signal(String, T)` | named (names surface in dependency errors) |
212: | `signal(initial, equal)` | `Signals.signal(T, BiPredicate<T,T>)` | custom equality |
213: | `computed(fn)` | `Signals.computed(Supplier<T>)` | lazy, memoized derived signal |
214: | `effect(fn)` | `Signals.effect(Runnable)` | runs immediately, then on dependency change |
215: | `untracked(fn)` | `Signals.untracked(Supplier<T>)` | reads without recording dependencies |
216: | `read()` | `get()` | current value |
217: | `write(v)` | `set(T)` | replace (no-op when equal) |
218: | `update(fn)` | `update(UnaryOperator<T>)` | derive from current and write |
219: | `asReadonly()` | `asReadonly()` | read-only view of a writable signal |
220: 
221: **Guarantees** (must be preserved by any implementation): equality suppression,
222: synchronous flush at the end of the outermost write, glitch-free propagation
223: (each computed recomputes at most once per flush), error caching, write
224: discipline, and circular-dependency detection.
225: 
226: ### 3.2 Two-way binding
227: 
228: A control's value is **a `WritableSignal<T>` supplied as a config value**:
229: `TextField.with(t -> t.placeholder("…").text(writable))`,
230: `Toggle.with(t -> t.isOn(writable))`,
231: `Slider.with(s -> s.value(writable).min(0).max(100))`. The flow:
232: 
233: 1. At **mount**, the DSL control records a **value input** (a sink on the
234:    retained node) for the signal, and the emitter exposes routing registries to
235:    the host: tap actions, text inputs, value inputs, date inputs.
236: 2. The host receives the control's raw event (`TEXT_CHANGED`,
237:    `VALUE_CHANGED`, `DATE_CHANGED`, or a composed tap) and calls the sink,
238:    which **writes into the signal**.
239: 3. The signal flush re-emits **only that node's** delta (`SET_TEXT`,
240:    `SET_PROPERTY`, `SET_DATE`) back through the emitter.
241: 
242: Reading is equally fine-grained: a node's text or a property value can be
243: **bound to a signal** — `Text.with(t -> t.text(signal))`,
244: `.modifiers(ForegroundStyle.with(f -> f.color(colorSignal)), FontSize.with(s -> s.size(sizeSignal)))`
245: — so a change re-emits only the bound node.
246: 
247: ### 3.3 Persisted state (`State<T>`)
248: 
249: A `State<T>` field is the SwiftUI-`@State`-shaped form of a persisted signal,
250: **auto-wired by key**:
251: 
252: ```java
253: State<Integer> count = new State<>(0);            // key = field name "count"
254: State<Integer> total = new State<>(0, "total");   // explicit store key
255: count.get(); count.set(0); count.update(v -> v + 1);
256: count.signal();                                   // the WritableSignal (for TextField, …)
257: ```
258: 
259: The store (`StateStore`) is untyped and platform-neutral (in-memory, Redis,
260: file, SQLite, LocalStorage, NVS flash). The Java realization wires `State`
261: fields via an annotation processor that generates a `<View>_StateBinder` per
262: view class; connection happens when the view renders. A generated DSL in a
263: language without reflection/annotation processing MUST offer the equivalent
264: explicit wiring.
265: 
266: ### 3.4 Structural reactivity (conditional rendering)
267: 
268: The tree is normally static once mounted (["`body()` is evaluated once at
269: mount"](#1-design-principles-dsl-flavored)); the **only** sanctioned way to
270: change *structure* reactively is a **structural container**: a slot whose
271: single child subtree is selected by a signal and **reconciled** when the
272: signal changes. This is the foundation for `if`/`else`, `switch`, and
273: navigation ([§4.5](#45-navigation)).
274: 
275: | Canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) | Java DSL | Rust DSL | Emits |
276: |----------------------------|----------|----------|-------|
277: | `if cond { then } else { else }` in a result builder | `Conditional.when(Signal<Boolean>, View then, View else)` | plain `if`/`match` in `build()` | `TREE` deltas (reconcile) |
278: | `switch value { case a -> v; default -> d }` | `Conditional.when(Signal<T>, Case.of(T, View)...)` + `Case.otherwise(View)` | plain `if`/`match` in `build()` | `TREE` deltas (reconcile) |
279: 
280: **Java realization** (`com.pathland.view.Conditional`): statically importable
281: lowercase factories on a final class with a private constructor, mirroring
282: [`Signals`](#31-signal-surface):
283: 
284: ```java
285: import static com.pathland.view.Conditional.when;
286: import static com.pathland.view.Conditional.Case;
287: 
288: when(showLogin, new LoginView(), new HomeView());           // if / else
289: when(mode,
290:     Case.of(RouteMode.HOME, new HomeView()),
291:     Case.of(RouteMode.USERS, new UsersView()),
292:     Case.otherwise(new NotFoundView()));                     // switch + default
293: ```

296: `when` (Kotlin's `switch` analog, and a valid Java identifier) is the method
297: name, and `Case.of(...)` / `Case.otherwise(...)` carry the branches. A boolean

299: signal takes keyed `Case` branches typed to the signal's value type, with an

301: `.of(...)` survives — they are not views or modifiers but statically-imported

308:    selected content. Selection is a **content function** over the selector
309:    signal — `if`/`else` and `switch` are sugar over it, so value-parametrized
310:    content (e.g. a route param) is a first-class case.
311: 2. On selector change the container re-evaluates the content function,
312:    **renders the new subtree**, and the emitter **reconciles** it against the
313:    retained snapshot — emitting only `TREE` deltas (`CREATE_NODE` /
314:    `DELETE_NODE` / `INSERT_CHILD` / `REMOVE_CHILD` / `MOVE_CHILD`).
315: 3. **Identical structure emits zero opcodes.** The reconcile diffs old vs new;
316:    a recompute that yields the same structure produces no `TREE` deltas, so no
317:    equality predicate is needed on the selector signal.
318: 4. Structural containers **nest**: a container inside a container re-evaluates
319:    and reconciles its own slot independently.
320: 5. All other reactivity stays fine-grained (`SET_TEXT` / `SET_PROPERTY`); a
321:    structural container never re-emits siblings or ancestors.
322: 
323: **Rust delta**: the Rust DSL builds `Node` trees directly and the host rebuilds
324: + re-`assign_id`s + diffs on every interaction, so plain `if`/`match` in

content.text:
Good catch — this is a real hole. Here's what I found.

## The gap is in the API, not the machinery
The emitter already supports binding *any* supported property to a signal:
- `Modified.Prop.reactive` → `node.propertyBindings`, and `ReactiveValues.from` accepts `Boolean`/`Integer`/`Float`/`String`/`Color` (emitter `registerNodeBindings` turns each non-constant binding into a node-level effect).
- `ConstantSignal` short-circuits, so a literal carries zero binding overhead.

But the config surface only exposes `Signal<T>` setters for ~8 members: `Text.text`, `Image/Audio/Video.source`, `Icon.name`, `Label.title/icon`, `Background.color`, `AccessibilityLabel.text`, `FontSize.size`, `ForegroundStyle.color`. Everything else stores raw primitives, so `Visible`/`Disabled`/`Opacity`/`Padding`/`Border`/transforms literally cannot be made reactive. Your example is exactly the worst case: `visible(boolean)` has no signal path.

Rust chose a different spelling: a generic `Bound` modifier + typed `FontSize::bound(sig)` etc., rather than signal-consuming config members. So there's also a cross-language inconsistency to settle.

## Contract options
- **A — Uniform signals-first config.** Every value member gets `foo(raw)` + `foo(Signal<T>)`; the raw setter wraps `Signals.constant`. Internally the config holds one `Signal<T>` (matches the AGENTS.md "single signal value convention"). Any property can react; identical emitter path; no wire change.
- **B — Curated reactive subset.** Only "app-mutable" values get signals (visibility, enabled, opacity, color, text, control values, progress/selection); structural/layout (padding, spacing, frame, alignment, columns/tracks) stay raw. Smaller surface, but an arbitrary line — you couldn't animate padding.
- **C — Opt-in `Bound` modifier (Rust's model).** Configs stay raw; a generic `Bound.with(b -> b.property(p).signal(s))` binds any node property, with typed helpers. One mechanism, but two ways to express color/text and it bypasses the config convention.

## Sub-decisions either way
1. Internal representation: always one `Signal<T>` field, literals via `Signals.constant` (recommended; zero-cost when constant).
2. Two-way vs one-way: control values take `WritableSignal<T>`; display/modifier properties take `Signal<T>`. Since `WritableSignal extends Signal`, overload resolution stays clean.
3. Java overload shape: `uniform(float)` + `uniform(Signal<Float>)`.
4. `Signal` is a `@FunctionalInterface`, so a raw lambda is accepted but *not* a `ConstantSignal` → would register a no-op effect. Raw overloads must be preferred for literals; worth documenting.
5. Cross-language parity: make Rust configs signal-capable too, or keep `Bound` as Rust's documented realization. Spec §2 currently only says "raw or Signal" loosely — adopting A makes it a MUST per member.

My recommendation is **A** (it's arguably just finishing what §2 already intends, and it kills the whole class of "this property can't react" holes), keeping control values two-way. Cost: touch every config (~50 modifiers, ~40 views) — but we're already rewriting them, so it's mostly additive overloads, and no protocol/no_std impact.

Locked in: **uniform signals-first configs**, internally one `Signal<T>` per value member, and **unify Rust on the same contract**. Here's the plan.

## Spec (`spec/DSL.md`) — first
- **§2**: make it a MUST — every value member of a config accepts a raw value **or** a `Signal<T>`; the raw setter is sugar for `Signals.constant(...)`. A non-constant signal becomes a node-level `SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY` binding; a constant emits as a plain property (zero binding overhead). Control *values* take `WritableSignal<T>` (two-way); all other value members take `Signal<T>` (one-way).
- **§3.1/§3.2**: state the single-signal convention (one `Signal<T>` field per value) and note `WritableSignal extends Signal` so overloads resolve by specificity.
- **§5**: add a one-line rule instead of per-row duplication ("every value member below has a raw + `Signal<T>` form"), plus the `Signal` `@FunctionalInterface` caveat (literals go through the raw overload).
- **§9.3**: Rust realization = same contract (`impl Into<Reactive<T>>` on builder setters); `Bound`/`*.bound` fold into it (kept as sugar or removed).
- **§10** status delta.

## Java — `lib/java/pathland-view`
1. **Plumbing** (`emit`): add `PathlandNode.property(int id, Signal<?>)` — sets the value and, when non-constant, records a `propertyBindings` entry; use it from both views and `Modified`. 13: /**
14:  * An {@link OpcodeSink} that accumulates a self-contained {@link ProtocolFrame} (opcodes +
15:  * string section) entirely in the JVM. This is the SSR / WebSocket path: the frame is
16:  * rendered to HTML or encoded to the network batch wire format.
17:  */
18: public class FrameOpcodeSink implements OpcodeSink {
19: 
20:     private final List<Opcode> opcodes = new ArrayList<>();
21:     private final ByteArrayOutputStream strings = new ByteArrayOutputStream();
22:     private ProtocolFrame frame = ProtocolFrame.EMPTY;
23:     private int framesProduced;
24: 
25:     /** The frame built by the last {@code beginFrame/endFrame} pair. */
26:     public ProtocolFrame frame() {
27:         return frame;
28:     }
29: 
30:     /** Number of completed frames so far (unchanged signals do not produce a frame). */
31:     public int framesProduced() {
32:         return framesProduced;
33:     }
34: 
35:     public boolean hasChanges() {
36:         return !opcodes.isEmpty();
37:     }
38: 
39:     @Override
40:     public void beginFrame() {
41:         opcodes.clear();
42:         strings.reset();
43:     }
44: 
45:     @Override
46:     public void endFrame() {
47:         frame = new ProtocolFrame(List.copyOf(opcodes), strings.toByteArray());
48:         framesProduced++;
49:     }
50: 
51:     @Override
52:     public void createNode(int id, int component) {
53:         push(Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.CREATE_NODE, 0, id, component, 0);
54:     }
55: 
56:     @Override
57:     public void deleteNode(int id) {
58:         push(Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.DELETE_NODE, 0, id, 0, 0);
59:     }
60: 
61:     @Override
62:     public void insertChild(int parent, int child, int index) {
63:         push(Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.INSERT_CHILD, 0, parent, child, index);
64:     }
65: 
66:     @Override
67:     public void removeChild(int parent, int child) {
68:         push(Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.REMOVE_CHILD, 0, parent, child, 0);
69:     }
70: 
71:     @Override
72:     public void moveChild(int parent, int child, int newIndex) {
73:         push(Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.MOVE_CHILD, 0, parent, child, newIndex);
74:     }
75: 
76:     @Override
77:     public void setText(int nodeId, String text) {
78:         int offset = strings.size();
79:         writeString(text);
80:         push(Categories.PARAMETER, Commands.Parameter.SET_TEXT, 0, nodeId, offset, 0);
81:     }
82: 
83:     @Override
84:     public void setProperty(int nodeId, int property, int valueType, Object value) {
85:         int b = (valueType << 16) | (property & 0xFFFF);
86:         if (valueType == ValueTypes.STRING) {
87:             int offset = strings.size();
88:             writeString((String) value);
89:             push(Categories.PARAMETER, Commands.Parameter.SET_PROPERTY, 0, nodeId, b, offset);
90:         } else if (valueType == ValueTypes.DESIGN_TOKEN) {
91:             // C = arena offset of the token path (spec/TOKENS.md).
92:             int offset = strings.size();
93:             writeString(((Color) value).token());
94:             push(Categories.PARAMETER, Commands.Parameter.SET_PROPERTY, 0, nodeId, b, offset);
95:         } else if (valueType == ValueTypes.LIST) {
96:             // C = arena offset of a length-prefixed array `[u32 count][f32 × count]`
97:             // (spec/OPCODE.md §Value types — a `FIT_QUERY` threshold table).
98:             int offset = strings.size();
99:             float[] elements = (float[]) value;
100:             writeIntLE(elements.length);
101:             for (float element : elements) {
102:                 strings.write(Float.floatToIntBits(element) & 0xFF);
103:                 strings.write((Float.floatToIntBits(element) >>> 8) & 0xFF);
104:                 strings.write((Float.floatToIntBits(element) >>> 16) & 0xFF);
105:                 strings.write((Float.floatToIntBits(element) >>> 24) & 0xFF);
106:             }
107:             push(Categories.PARAMETER, Commands.Parameter.SET_PROPERTY, 0, nodeId, b, offset);
108:         } else {
109:             push(Categories.PARAMETER, Commands.Parameter.SET_PROPERTY, 0, nodeId, b, ValueEncoder.encodeBits(valueType, value));
110:         }
111:     }

115:         push(Categories.PARAMETER, Commands.Parameter.SET_DATE, 0, nodeId, days, millisOfDay);
116:     }
117: 
118:     @Override
119:     public void setDesignToken(String path, int valueType, Object value) {
120:         int pathOffset = strings.size();
121:         writeString(path);
122:         int c;
123:         if (valueType == ValueTypes.STRING) {
124:             c = strings.size();
125:             writeString((String) value);
126:         } else {
127:             c = ValueEncoder.encodeBits(valueType, value);
128:         }
129:         push(Categories.PARAMETER, Commands.Parameter.SET_DESIGN_TOKEN, 0, pathOffset, valueType, c);
130:     }
131: 
132:     /** Append a length-prefixed string to the string section, returning its offset. */
133:     public int writeString(String text) {
134:         int offset = strings.size();
135:         byte[] utf8 = text.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
136:         writeIntLE(utf8.length);
137:         strings.writeBytes(utf8);
138:         return offset;
139:     }

141:     private void push(int category, int command, int flags, int a, int b, int c) {
142:         opcodes.add(new Opcode(category, command, flags, a, b, c));
143:     }
144: 
145:     private void writeIntLE(int value) {
146:         strings.write(value & 0xFF);
147:         strings.write((value >>> 8) & 0xFF);
148:         strings.write((value >>> 16) & 0xFF);
149:         strings.write((value >>> 24) & 0xFF);
150:     }

Yes — **compact first**. The work is fully committed (`15b654dd`, `416a88e1`, `ac39bb82` on `spec/dsl-v2-authoring-surface`, clean tree), so nothing is lost, and a fresh context will make the large Phase 3 pass much safer.

Here's the Phase 3 plan to carry into the next context.

## Phase 3 — migrate consumers, then cut the bridges

**Goal:** every call site on the v2 surface (`with`/`modifiers`/`children`, signals-first), then delete the legacy `.of(...)` factories, `View.with(ViewModifier...)` + `View` sugar (`font`/`environment`/`buttonStyle`/`onPathChange`/`navigate`/`push`/`replace`), and the 15 `*Mod`/`FontMod` shims. `mvn install` green at the end.

**Chunks (each keeps the reactor compiling until the final cut):**
1. **Library-internal call sites** (`pathland-view` itself): `Label.body` (`Text.of`/`Image.of`/`Button.of`/`Group.of`/`content.with(AccessibilityLabel.of(…))`), `LabelStyle` built-ins, `BorderedButtonStyle`, `ButtonStyleMod`/`EnvironmentMod` internals, `NavigationLink` (`Button.of`), `PlainButtonStyle`. Migrate to the new API (compiles against the bridge).
2. **Consumers:** `pathland-demo-views` (~420 `.of`/170 `.with`), `pathland-server-core` (~80), `pathland-render-html` (~40), `pathland-spring/quarkus-starter`, `*-demo`s, and the library's own tests (`EmitterTest`, `FrameTest`, `LabelTest`, `IconTest`, `SizeThatFitsTest`, `RouterTest`, …). Mechanical rewrite: `Text.of("x").with(FontSize.of(24), FontWeightMod.of(BOLD))` → `Text.with(t -> t.text("x")).modifiers(FontSize.with(s -> s.size(24)), FontWeight.BOLD)`; `Slider.of(sig,0,100)` → `Slider.with(s -> s.value(sig).min(0).max(100))`; `ButtonStyleMod.of(style)` → `.modifiers(style)`.
3. **Route-intent sugar** — decide: keep `.navigate/.push/.replace` as builder methods on `ViewBuilder`/`View` (spec §4.5 "any component can change the route"), or route everything through `NavigationLink.with(...)`. Recommend keeping a `NavigationLink` + a nav-intent modifier value; drop the `View` instance sugar.
4. **Keep as factory functions (not the bridge):** `Conditional.when`/`Case.of`/`Case.otherwise` (§3.4 explicitly), `Color.of(int)`/`rgb/argb/token`, `SizeThatFits.of`/`Fit.of`, `Signals.*`, `Frame.ofWidth/ofHeight` etc. (now delegating to `Frame.with`). Convert `NavigationContainer` → `NavigationContainer.with(n -> n.router(r))` per spec §10.
5. **Cut:** remove the bridge methods + `*Mod`/`FontMod` shims (`AudioStyleMod`, `ButtonStyleMod`, `ControlSizeMod`, `EnvironmentMod`, `FontDesignMod`, `FontStyleMod`, `FontMod`, `FontWeightMod`, `LabelStyleMod`, `NavigationMod`, `PathChangeMod`, `TextAlignmentMod`, `TextCaseMod`, `TruncationMod`, `VideoStyleMod`) — repurposing `EnvironmentMod`/`PathChangeMod`/`NavigationMod` as modifier values if needed. Fix compile fallout; run `cd lib/java && mvn install`.
6. **Docs:** update `AGENTS.md` (Java DSL still documents `.of(...)`), `lib/java/*/status.md`, spec §10 status delta.

**Risks:** library-internal `.of` usage means the final cut touches `pathland-view` itself in the same commit; the demo-views migration is large but mechanical; `View` sugar removal may surface usages in `pathland-server-core`/SSR.

**Verification:** `mvn -o -pl pathland-view test` stays green per chunk, then full `cd lib/java && mvn install`; Rust `cargo test --workspace` unaffected.

Good to compact now — I'll resume with chunk 1 (library-internal) after.

## Objective
- Complete the DSL v2 migration per `spec/DSL.md`: the Java library (`lib/java/pathland-view`) is being migrated to the `with`/`modifiers`/`children` authoring surface; Rust has been brought to parity on the same contract; consumers (demo-views, server-core, render-html, starters, tests) still need migration, after which legacy `.of`/`View.with`/`*Mod` shims are removed.
- A parallel effort changed the reactivity contract: **uniform signals-first configs** — every config value member takes a raw value or a `Signal<T>` (raw is sugar for `Signals.constant`); a non-constant signal is a node-level binding; control values take `WritableSignal<T>` (two-way), everything else one-way `Signal<T>`. Applied to spec, Java, and Rust.

## Important Details
- Working branch: `spec/dsl-v2-authoring-surface` (not pushed). Commits this session: `50335f13` (Java v2 infra + ViewBuilder), `15b654dd` (v2 views/modifiers/value-is-modifier), `416a88e1` (signals-first spec + Java; Rust phase in progress, uncommitted).
- User decisions (locked): uniform signals-first configs; **all** value members reactive (layout included: spacing/alignment/padding/frame/columns/tracks); control values two-way `WritableSignal`; unify Rust on same contract; **remove** Rust `Bound`/`*.bound`; implementation order spec → Java → Rust.
- Java: implementations are additive — legacy `.of(...)` and `View.with(ViewModifier...)` are kept as a temporary bridge (final surface is the hard cut: remove them + redundant `*Mod` shims at the end). `View` keeps only `body()`/`render()` (+ nested `Config`); the `ViewBuilder<V,C>` holds the chain (Java static-hides-instance rule: statics are on view classes).
- Spec (`spec/DSL.md`) now: §2 MUST — every value member accepts raw or `Signal<T>`; §3.1 one-signal-per-value; §5.0 raw+Signal rule + `@FunctionalInterface` caveat (literals must use the raw overload, else a bare lambda registers a harmless reactive binding); §9.3 Rust `impl IntoReactive<T>`/`Bound` removed; §10 updated.
- Java plumbing: `PathlandNode.property(int id, Signal<?>)` sets the value and records a `propertyBindings` entry for non-constant signals; `emit.ReactiveValues.from` now coerces via `ValueTypes.forProperty` (F32→float, U8/U32/I32/ENUM→int, COLOR/STRING/DESIGN_TOKEN passthrough) and maps `WireValue` enums to their numeric code. `WireValue` marker implemented by: Alignment, HorizontalAlignment, VerticalAlignment, ShapeKind, ContentMode, ToggleStyle, PickerStyle, DatePickerMode, FontWeight, FontStyle, FontDesign, ControlSize, TextCase, Truncation, TextAlignment.
- Rust engine limitation (relevant for remaining Rust work): `SignalValueKind` is implemented for `f32`, `u32`, `bool`, `u8`, `String` only — `Align`/`Color` are not signal kinds, so reactive alignment/color binding via typed signals isn't expressible; those Rust config members remain static.
- Do NOT run workspace-wide `cargo fmt` (repo is not rustfmt-clean). `lib/rust/check-wasm.sh` must stay green (pathland-core/engine/view are `#![no_std]` + alloc).
- Java module test command: `mvn -o -pl pathland-view test` (currently **143 green** — 136 + 7 `ReactiveConfigTest`). Rust test command: `cd lib/rust && cargo test --workspace`.

## Work State
### Completed
- **Spec (Phase 0)**: `spec/DSL.md` signals-first MUST + §9.3 Rust `IntoReactive`, Bound removed (committed in `416a88e1`).
- **Java (Phase 1)**: all view configs and all modifier configs converted to store one `Signal<T>` per value with raw + Signal setters; `PathlandNode.property(id, Signal)`, `ReactiveValues` type-coercion + `WireValue` support; `Disabled` uses `Signals.computed` for the enabled inverse; `Frame` normalizes `±∞`→FILL reactively; `Padding` edges are per-edge `Signal<Float>`; control values stay `WritableSignal`. Tests: `ViewBuilderTest`, `ModifierWithTest`, `ReactiveConfigTest`. `lib/java/pathland-view/status.md` updated. Committed as `416a88e1`.
- **Rust (Phase 2, near-complete but uncommitted)**: added `Reactive<T>`/`IntoReactive<T>` (impls for `T`, `Signal<T>`, `WritableSignal<T>`) + helpers `reactive_f32`, `reactive_enum`, `reactive_u32`, `reactive_color` in `lib/rust/crates/pathland-view/src/lib.rs`; converted modifiers (Padding, FontSize, ForegroundStyle, Background, Tint, Opacity, Border, CornerRadius, FontWeight, LineLimit, TextAlignment, TruncationMode, Offset, Position, ZIndex) to named structs + same-name `#[allow(non_snake_case)] pub fn X(value: impl IntoReactive<...>) -> X`; removed `Bound` + the five `*.bound` conveniences; updated the `property_binds_to_a_signal` test to `FontSize(size)`; converted StackConfig (spacing), GridConfig (columns/rows/spacing), `grid_apply`, ProgressViewConfig (value), GaugeConfig (value/min/max + manual `Default`). `cargo build -p pathland-view` green.

### Active
- Fixing the Rust test compile error: `grid_config_emits_counts` (`Grid::with(|g| g.columns(2).rows(3).spacing(4.0))` in `lib.rs` tests) fails because integer literals don't satisfy `impl IntoReactive<f32>` (blanket impl is only `IntoReactive<T> for T`). Options: change the test to `g.columns(2.0).rows(3.0)` (grep shows this is the only `.columns(`/`.rows(` call site in the workspace), or add `impl IntoReactive<f32> for u32`-style conversions.

### Blocked
- Rust Phase 2 not yet verified: must run `cargo test --workspace` + `lib/rust/check-wasm.sh` and update `lib/rust/crates/pathland-view/status.md` and `pathland-engine/status.md`.

## Next Move
1. Fix the Rust test: change `lib.rs` test `grid_config_emits_counts` to `g.columns(2.0).rows(3.0).spacing(4.0)` (or add integer→f32 `IntoReactive` impls), then `cd lib/rust && cargo test --workspace`.
2. Run `lib/rust/check-wasm.sh`; update `lib/rust/crates/pathland-view/status.md` + `pathland-engine/status.md`; commit "feat(dsl): signals-first configs — Rust (reactive members, Bound removed)".
3. Phase 3: migrate consumers (`lib/java/pathland-demo-views`, `pathland-server-core`, `pathland-render-html`, starters, `*-demo`, tests) to `with`/`modifiers`/`children` + signal configs; then remove the legacy `.of`/`View.with` bridge and the redundant `*Mod` shims (`FontWeightMod`, `TextAlignmentMod`, `TruncationMod`, `TextCaseMod`, `ControlSizeMod`, `FontDesignMod`, `FontStyleMod`, `FontMod`, `AudioStyleMod`, `VideoStyleMod`, `ButtonStyleMod`, `LabelStyleMod`, `EnvironmentMod`, `NavigationMod`, `PathChangeMod`); verify with `mvn install` from `lib/java` and the Java consumer tests; docs step (AGENTS.md).

## Relevant Files
- `spec/DSL.md`: signals-first contract (MUST §2, §3.1, §5.0, §9.3, §10).
- `lib/java/pathland-view/src/main/java/com/pathland/view/{View,ViewBuilder,Configurable,ChildrenView,WireValue}.java`: v2 infrastructure + WireValue marker.
- `lib/java/pathland-view/src/main/java/com/pathland/view/emit/{PathlandNode,ReactiveValues,ValueEncoder,ValueTypes}.java`: property-binding path and type coercion.
- `lib/java/pathland-view/src/main/java/com/pathland/view/`: all view/modifier classes converted to signals-first (Text, VStack/HStack/ZStack/Grid/Lazy*, ProgressView, Gauge, controls, every modifier; value-is-modifier enums FontWeight/TextAlignment/Truncation/TextCase/ControlSize/FontStyle/FontDesign; Font and Style as modifiers).
- `lib/java/pathland-view/src/test/java/com/pathland/view/{ViewBuilderTest,ModifierWithTest,ReactiveConfigTest}.java`.
- `lib/java/pathland-view/status.md`: updated (signals-first; 143 tests).
- `lib/rust/crates/pathland-view/src/lib.rs`: `Reactive`/`IntoReactive` + `reactive_*` helpers; converted modifiers; StackConfig/GridConfig/ProgressViewConfig/GaugeConfig; `Bound` removed; failing test `grid_config_emits_counts` line 3673.
- `lib/rust/crates/pathland-engine/src/{signal.rs,engine.rs,node.rs}`: `SignalValueKind` (f32/u32/bool/u8/String), `SignalId`/`IntoSignalId`, property-binding resolution.
- `lib/rust/crates/pathland-view/status.md`, `pathland-engine/status.md`: Rust status not yet updated.
- Deferred Java views still `.of`-only: `SizeThatFits`, `Conditional`, `NavigationContainer`, `NavigationLink`, `Color` (record).

85: - **Modifiers are decoupled from views — and never hard-bound to a view
86:   type.** Any modifier applies to any view (`.padding` works on a `Text` and a
87:   `VStack` alike), and any developer can **author a custom modifier in
88:   application code** (a `ViewModifier`) that applies to any existing view —
89:   library primitive, container, control, custom view, or an already-modified
90:   view (see [§5.6](#56-custom-modifiers-developer-authored)). A modifier a
91:   given renderer cannot apply is **allowed and ignored** — the property is
92:   still emitted.
93: - **There is exactly one modifier mechanism.** Built-in core modifiers are
94:   **not** a separate syntax: they are `ViewModifier` values the library ships,
95:   composed into a view through the shared `modifiers(...)` operation. There is
96:   **no per-modifier sugar on the view type** — `Padding` applied via
97:   `.modifiers(Padding.with(p -> p.uniform(16)))`. Core and application-authored
98:   modifiers share the same surface.
99: - **A modifier's type is named for the modifier it applies — never with a
100:   `Mod` suffix.** Where a modifier applies a single value (a font, a font
101:   weight, an alignment, a style), the value type itself MAY *be* the modifier
102:   (`FontWeight.BOLD`, `Font.headline()`, `MyButtonStyle`), so there is one name
103:   for the concept. Languages that cannot merge the two (e.g. C#, whose enums
104:   cannot implement interfaces) use the equivalent value form. See
105:   [§9.3](#93-language-adaptation-rules).
106: - **There is exactly one style mechanism.** A customizable control/view takes
107:   its **content** from a *style* value (`ButtonStyle`, `LabelStyle`,
108:   `AudioStyle`, `VideoStyle`, …) scoped through the environment; the control
109:   owns its native component + interaction and the style owns the content
110:   ([§5.7](#57-styleable-controls-the-style-contract)). Closed-variant/token
111:   styles (`ToggleStyle`, `PickerStyle`, `TextStyle`) are the same surface.
112: - **Values vs modifiers.** Structural/layout parameters and a control's bound
113:   value (`alignment`, `spacing`, `text`, `isOn`, `selection`) are **values**
114:   configured through `with(...)`. Everything decorative (padding, color, font,
115:   frame, border, …) is a **modifier** applied through `modifiers(...)`.
116: - **`Color` is never a modifier.** `Color` has SwiftUI's dual identity: it is a
117:   **View** (a layout-greedy solid-color fill) and a **Data Type** (passed into
118:   style-taking modifiers: `.foregroundStyle`, `.background`, `.border`,
119:   `.tint`). There is **no** `.color()` modifier, and `.foregroundColor(_:)` is
120:   deprecated — foreground styling is always `.foregroundStyle(_:)`.
121: - **Only changes are transmitted.** Emission is diff-based; an unchanged tree
122:   emits **zero** opcodes. The DSL describes values; the emitter diffs them.
123: - **Typed enums, never raw ints.** Every enumerated value is a typed constant
124:   (`Alignment.leading`, `FontWeight.bold`, `ToggleStyle.checkbox`), not a bare
125:   integer. The numeric code is the DSL's job to resolve (see the value-type and
126:   enum tables in MODIFIERS.md).

130: ## 2. Canonical signature notation
131: 
132: The canonical signatures below are written SwiftUI-shaped and language
133: agnostic. Conventions used:
134: 
135: - `View(config:)` / `T("…")` — a view/control constructed with its **values**.
136: - `{ ... }` — the child subtree (a trailing closure in SwiftUI; a vararg,
137:   macro, builder, or lambda in other languages).
138: - `Signal<T>` — a read-only derived or writable signal; `WritableSignal<T>` —
139:   a two-way binding target. A control takes a `WritableSignal<T>` for its
140:   value (see [§3](#3-state-model-signals)).
141: - `()` — the action a `Button` fires.
142: - `.modifier(m)` — apply a **modifier value** to a view; chainable on any
143:   view. Every modifier — built-in or application-authored — is such a value
144:   ([§5.6](#56-custom-modifiers-developer-authored)).
145: - Modifiers chain and are applied **innermost-first** (the last chained
146:   modifier's property wins).
147: 
148: ### The three operations
149: 
150: Every concrete view exposes the same three operations. They form one fluent
151: **builder**: any of the three may be the first call, and they may be chained in
152: any order. A later call overrides an earlier value for the same property.
153: 
154: | Operation | Purpose | Canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) |
155: |-----------|---------|----------------------------|
156: | **values** | Configure structural/layout values and a control's bound value | `View(config:)` — labels in the constructor |
157: | **modifiers** | Apply `ViewModifier` values, innermost-first | `.modifier(_:)` / `.padding(_:)` / … |
158: | **children** | Supply the content subtree (content-bearing views only) | trailing closure `{ … }` |
159: 
160: The **canonical builder spelling** (the recommended form; per-language spellings
161: are in [§9.3](#93-language-adaptation-rules)) is:
162: 
163: ```
164: ViewName.with { values }              // values   — a config-builder lambda
165:       .modifiers(modifier, ...)       // modifiers — varargs
166:       .children(view, ...)            // children  — varargs, content-bearing views only
167: ```
168: 
169: Any of the three may start the chain, e.g. all of these are equivalent:
170: 
171: ```
172: VStack.with { v in v.spacing(8) }.children(a, b).modifiers(m)
173: VStack.children(a, b).with { v in v.spacing(8) }.modifiers(m)
174: VStack.modifiers(m).children(a, b).with { v in v.spacing(8) }
175: ```
176: 
177: **Values are a config-builder lambda.** `with { c in … }` populates a per-view
178: fluent **config** (`VStack.Config`, `Text.Config`, …). It is the *same type* a
179: style's `makeBody(Config)` receives ([§5.7](#57-styleable-controls-the-style-contract)).
180: The builder is **fluent and mutable**: setters return the config. Config-less
181: views (`Divider`, `Spacer`) take an empty `with()`.
182: 
183: **Every value member is reactive-capable (MUST).** A config member that carries a
184: value exposes **two forms** — a raw value and a `Signal<T>`:
185: 
186: ```
187: Text.with(t -> t.text("hi"))            ≡  Text.with(t -> t.text(constant("hi")))
188: Visible.with(v -> v.visible(flagSignal))      // reactive visibility
189: Frame.with(f -> f.width(widthSignal))         // reactive sizing, layout included
190: ```
191: 
192: The **raw form is sugar for a constant signal**; a **non-constant** signal
193: becomes a **node-level binding** — a change re-emits only that node's `SET_TEXT`
194: / `SET_PROPERTY`, and a constant emits as a plain property with **zero binding
195: overhead**. This holds for *every* value member, layout included
196: (`spacing`, `alignment`, `padding`, `frame`, `columns`, …): anything describable
197: in the protocol can animate. A control's two-way *value* takes a
198: `WritableSignal<T>`; every other member takes a one-way `Signal<T>`.
199: 
200: **Per-language realization.** Java cannot declare a static and an instance
201: method with the same signature, so the Java realization holds the three
202: statically on the view class and exposes the chainable forms on the returned
203: builder/view type. Other languages map the operations to their idioms
204: (extension methods, associated functions + traits, package constructors +
205: methods, kwargs) — see [§9.3](#93-language-adaptation-rules).
206: 
207: Per-language adaptation summary:
208: 
209: | Language | Case | Composition mechanism | Example |
